title: Container supply-chain hardening: pinned CUDA/driver lockstep and SBOM sync
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: establish a robust dependency & artifact management flow that enforces pinned CUDA/driver stacks, produces attested SBOMs, and gates rollouts by artifact provenance and compatibility. Scope covers container build/promotion pipelines for hosted and Dedicated images, SBOM generation/attestation, CUDA/driver compatibility matrix, and integration of artifact checks into rollout gates (canary, A/B, automatic rollback). Excludes changes to end-user model packaging; separate follow-up will track model artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: All production container images must include a machine-readable SBOM (CycloneDX) produced at build time and signed with our release key.
Image tag format includes semver + runtime-lts channel + cuda-major.minor + short-sha (eg 2.4.0+lts-2026.03+cuda11.8+g7a2c)

CUDA and NVIDIA driver versions are recorded in image labels and matched to a driver compatibility matrix; upgrade pipeline rejects images incompatible with pinned host driver ranges for Dedicated/Private nodes.
Cosign-based image signatures and SBOM attestation are verified by the rollout gate; failures abort canary promotion automatically.
Rollout console shows SBOM diff and CVE delta for every candidate, with a human-acknowledge gate for high-severity regressions.
Documentation and runbook for rolling back an incompatible driver or image are published in Confluence and linked from the Console deployment page.
work_items: Add SBOM generation step to the base image pipeline using syft -> CycloneDX format
Integrate cosign signing for images and SBOMs; store signatures in GCR artifact metadata
Extend CI promotion job to compute and persist driver/CUDA metadata labels
Implement registry-level policy to prevent unsigned images from entering 'stable' LTS channel
Build a lightweight SBOM diff service that computes added/removed packages and cumulative CVE score
Add rollout-gate check that verifies SBOM signature, driver compatibility, and CVE delta before canary promotion
Create compatibility matrix (CSV) for CUDA major.minor vs host driver ranges and add validation test
Update Dedicated upgrade tooling to surface host-driver mismatch warnings and provide automatic node cordon/upgrade steps
decisions: Use CycloneDX for SBOMs to align with cloud vendor tooling and internal parsers
Adopt cosign for both image and SBOM signing to centralize trust roots and enable attestation verification
Tagging scheme will encode CUDA major.minor to make runtime compatibility explicit; we will avoid embedding full driver revision in tag to keep tags stable across micro-rebuilds
Registry-level promotion (candidate -> stable LTS) will be gated by signed SBOM + automated CVE threshold checks; human approval required for upgrades that change kernel-level drivers
risks: Tight locking of CUDA/driver versions could block urgent security kernel/driver updates for Dedicated customers
SBOM generation at scale increases build time and pipeline complexity; caching/remote SBOM artifact store required
False positives from CVE scanners may force manual intervention and slow rollouts
Private/on-prem deployments may require special handling due to air-gapped registries and custom host drivers
